lesson_title: One Phone, Ten Countries: The Global Economy
hook_text: The phone in your hand has probably visited about ten countries. Here is its journey.
clip_script: Designed in America or Korea. Chips made in Taiwan. Some of its metals possibly mined in Africa. Assembled in China. Shipped in a container to Durban. Trucked to your town. One phone, about ten countries. That is globalisation: countries joined together by trade, money, technology and people. Why not make everything here? Because every country is good at different things. We have platinum, coal and sunshine for oranges. Others are better at chips. Each specialises and swaps, and everyone ends up with more. But there is a catch at the border. The American factory wants dollars, not rand. At R18 a dollar, 50-dollar sneakers cost 900 rand. If the rand weakens to R20, they cost 1 000. Bad for shoppers. But good for our orange farmers, because our oranges just got cheaper for the rest of the world. That is the global economy: one big market, with winners and losers.
visual_style: A world map with an animated phone hopping between countries along dotted lines, then a simple exchange-rate counter flipping from R18 to R20 above a sneaker and an orange box.
pacing: Rapid map hops, a clear pause at the border, quick calculations on screen.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and work out what your favourite import costs at today's exchange rate.
